name: c-the-only-still-thing
prompt: Portrait-format antique glass-plate photograph from a studio camera planted dead level with an iron-and-slat park bench, the whole bench and its occupant filling the lower half, everything in deep focus. Seated squarely at the centre, facing the lens, is a heavy, corpulent gentleman of old money: a towering stovepipe hat with a glossy crown, a waistcoat buttoned tight across a vast round belly, a gold fob chain, spats, kid gloves, the right palm lifted level with his shoulder and flapping the world away. He is the only solid thing in the picture and he is pin-sharp, down to the nap of his hat and the pores of his jowls; his grin is broad, patient and fixed, the grin of someone who has held perfectly still for a hundred years, and his pale eyes stare straight out without a single blink. The plate was exposed in daylight for an impossibly long time, so every living thing that moved through the park has been erased into a faint vapour: a crowd of see-through streaks crossing in both directions, the half-there outline of a soldier leaning on a crutch, the washed-out silhouette of a nurse in scrubs, prams, dogs and drifting leaves, all layered and overlapping like breath on glass, some passing clean through the empty seat at his side; none of them leave a shadow, only he does, a hard black pool beneath the slats. Cold monochrome tones from charcoal to bone white, a dull diffuse overcast with no sun direction. The emulsion is dying: an iridescent blue-steel sheen bleeding inward from the dark edges, hairline scratches, flecks of dust, a corner chipped away to bare clear glass, a fine web of cracks. The upper third is a blank, faded, nearly white sky with two or three leafless twigs, left empty. Dread through stillness rather than gore. No text or lettering anywhere. Thanks.
